Simmer for 20 minutes. Heat butter in the skillet over medium-low heat. Add flour. Cook, stirring frequently, until flour browns, about 2 minutes. Add flour mixture to chile. Continue cooking and stirring until thickened to preference.

title: New Orleans Style Chicken Wing Dipping Sauce
ingredient_lines: 1 jar (12 ounces) of refrigerated chunky blue cheese dressing
⅓ cup scallions, finely chopped (reserve a teaspoon of chopped green tops for garnish)
steps: Combine all ingredients and refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving (overnight is preferable).
Garnish with the reserved scallions.
procedure_text: Combine all ingredients and refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving (overnight is preferable). Garnish with the reserved scallions.

title: New World Affogato
steps: Place the ice cream in a coffee cup.
Boil water in a pan, and then add coffee and sugar to it, and then mix well.
Add brandy to coffee mixture.
Pour coffee mixture over the ice-cream.
Serve immediately, garnished with cinnamon powder.
procedure_text: Place the ice cream in a coffee cup. Boil water in a pan, and then add coffee and sugar to it, and then mix well. Add brandy to coffee mixture. Pour coffee mixture over the ice-cream. Serve immediately, garnished with cinnamon powder.

title: New York City–Style Pizza
steps: Sprinkle the yeast over the surface of the warm water in a large bowl. Let stand for 1 minute, then stir to dissolve.
Mix in the flour, salt, and olive oil.
When the dough is too thick to stir, turn out onto a floured surface, and knead for 5 minutes. Knead in a little more flour if the dough is too sticky.
Place into an oiled bowl, cover, and set aside in a warm place to rise until doubled in bulk.

Preheat the oven to 550°F or as hot as your oven will go. Authentic New York pizzerias bake pizzas in ovens from 700–1,000°F. If using a pizza stone, preheat it in the oven as well, setting it on the lowest shelf.
When the dough has risen, flatten it out on a lightly floured surface.
Roll or stretch out into a 12-inch circle, and place on a baking sheet. If you are using a pizza stone, you may place the pizza on a piece of parchment while preheating the stone in the oven.
Spread the tomato sauce evenly over the dough. Sprinkle with oregano, mozzarella cheese, basil, Romano cheese, and red pepper flakes.
Bake for 12–15 minutes in the preheated oven, until the bottom of the crust is browned when you lift up the edge a little, and cheese is melted and bubbly.
Cool for about 5 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Ngoundja (Fried Plantains)
steps: Place the plantains on a cutting board, and use a knife to trim off both ends.
Make a shallow lengthwise incision along the skin of each plantain, being careful not to cut into the flesh.
Gently peel off the skin by using your fingers to lift it away from the flesh. If needed, you can use the knife to assist in peeling.
Lay the peeled plantains on the cutting board and cut them into diagonal or round slices, about ½ inch thick. You can adjust the thickness to your preference.
Pour enough vegetable oil into a deep frying pan or skillet to cover the bottom by about ¼ inch.

Place the pan over medium-high heat and allow the oil to become hot. You can test the temperature by dropping a small piece of plantain into the oil—if it sizzles immediately, the oil is ready for frying.

Carefully place the sliced plantains into the hot oil, making sure not to overcrowd the pan. Work in batches if necessary. Cook the plantains for about 2–3 minutes on each side or until they turn golden brown.
Use a slotted spoon to carefully remove the fried plantains from the pan and transfer them onto a plate lined with paper towels. This will help absorb any excess oil.
Sprinkle the fried plantains with a pinch of salt if desired, or leave them unsalted for a sweeter taste.
Allow the ngoundja to cool for a few minutes before serving to avoid burning your mouth. Serve as a side dish alongside your favorite main course, or enjoy them as a tasty snack on their own.

title: Nibbles
ingredient_lines: 2 boxes (16 cups/1 kg/2.2 lb) rice Chex cereal
1 box (8 cups/500 g/1.1 lb) wheat Chex cereal
steps: Melt and combine the sauce ingredients.
Combine all dry ingredients except salt in a large canning pot.
Sprinkle a little of the sauce mixture over dry ingredients, and shake well. Repeat until sauce is gone.
Salt the mixture by sprinkling and shaking in the same way.
Bake 1½–2 hours at 200 °F (95 °C) in covered canning pot.
Remove frequently to shake.
procedure_text: Melt and combine the sauce ingredients. Combine all dry ingredients except salt in a large canning pot. Sprinkle a little of the sauce mixture over dry ingredients, and shake well. Repeat until sauce is gone. Salt the mixture by sprinkling and shaking in the same way. Bake 1½–2 hours at 200 °F (95 °C) in covered canning pot. Remove frequently to shake.

title: Nigerian Barbecued Chicken Wings
steps: Combine the flour, cornmeal, pepper, salt, sugar, ginger, and paprika in a bowl.
Add the chicken pieces, and rub the mixture into them well so they are completely coated.
Set in the fridge, and allow the chicken to rest for 1 hour.
Arrange the chicken pieces on a baking tray or on a grill. Grill or bake until cooked through (about 45 minutes baking at 375°F).
procedure_text: Combine the flour, cornmeal, pepper, salt, sugar, ginger, and paprika in a bowl. Add the chicken pieces, and rub the mixture into them well so they are completely coated. Set in the fridge, and allow the chicken to rest for 1 hour. Arrange the chicken pieces on a baking tray or on a grill. Grill or bake until cooked through (about 45 minutes baking at 375°F).

title: Nigerian Bean Porridge
ingredient_lines: A few pieces of fresh tomato
Fresh scotch bonnet or habanero pepper
steps: Pick over the beans to remove stones and other unwanted items.
Put the beans in a clean bowl, and run under clean running water to wash them.
Boil water in a pot, and add the beans. Boil for 5 minutes, then strain and let run under cold water. Fully drain the beans.
Add the parboiled beans, chopped onion, palm oil, and bouillon cube to a pot. Cover with water, and simmer until the beans are tender.
Blend the crayfish, tomatoes, and pepper into a smooth paste.
Heat a pan. Add the tomato paste, panla fish, and salt/bouillon to taste. Fry for 5–7 minutes.
When the beans are soft and the water is reduced, stir in the fried paste and panla fish. Cook for 5–6 minutes.
Serve the beans porridge with pap (ogi), plantain (dodo), and/or bread.

title: Nigerian Boiled Fish
steps: Cut fresh fish into suitable sized pieces, and wash thoroughly. Remove unwanted substances inside the fish.
Put fish in a pot, cover with water, and add a pinch of salt.
Boil for a few minutes until cooked but tender.
procedure_text: Cut fresh fish into suitable sized pieces, and wash thoroughly. Remove unwanted substances inside the fish. Put fish in a pot, cover with water, and add a pinch of salt. Boil for a few minutes until cooked but tender.

title: Nigerian Boiled Plantain
steps: Boil some water in a pot, and add the plantain.
Cook for few minutes.
Serve with egg sauce, garden egg stew, or palm oil.
procedure_text: Boil some water in a pot, and add the plantain. Cook for few minutes. Serve with egg sauce, garden egg stew, or palm oil.

title: Nigerian Caramelized Coconut
steps: Carefully break open the coconut and reserve its juice.
Remove the coconut flesh from the shell, and grate it into small, thin pieces.
Combine the coconut juice and sugar in a pot. Stir in the grated coconut.
Add just enough water to cover the coconut.
Bring to a boil, stirring continuously.
Reduce to low heat, and continue stirring until the coconut pieces start browning and caramelizing.
Remove from the heat, and allow it to cool off.
procedure_text: Carefully break open the coconut and reserve its juice. Remove the coconut flesh from the shell, and grate it into small, thin pieces. Combine the coconut juice and sugar in a pot. Stir in the grated coconut. Add just enough water to cover the coconut. Bring to a boil, stirring continuously. Reduce to low heat, and continue stirring until the coconut pieces start browning and caramelizing. Remove from the heat, and allow it to cool off.

title: Nigerian Cassava Fufu
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a large pot. Stir in the cassava flour, working out any lumps.
Once the lumps are completely dissolved, add a small amount of water just above the cassava. Place the contents over a high to medium heat and stir intermittently.
The water will dry out after 10 minutes or longer of stirring, and the paste will thicken. Stir thoroughly until all of the whitish paste has combined and turned into a thick creamy tint.
Sprinkle water over it to keep it from becoming too thick, and flip it over to cook the other side. Scrape the edges of the pot and the wooden turner with a spoon if they appear hard and sticky.
When the fufu has softened and turned from a bright white to a creamy texture, remove it from the pot.
Place the cooked fufu on a flat surface or tray and set aside for 5 minutes to cool.
Hand-mix the fufu and roll it into balls like dough.

title: Nigerian Cauliflower Fufu
steps: Cut cauliflower into small pieces, and blend with a blender to give a purée.
Strain the cauliflower mixture through a cloth, retaining the solids.
Squeeze the sieve cloth to drain more water until relatively dry and a dough is formed.
Transfer the dough to a saucepan over medium heat, and stir in the psyllium husk.
Stir and mold to form a paste, and shape into portions.

Stir and mold to form a paste, and shape into portions.

title: Nigerian Cheesy Sausage Masa
steps: Grease the masa pan.
Fill each divot to the brim with the batter.
Bake in a preheated oven until puffed, golden, and cooked through.
Serve hot.
Heat the masa pan on the stovetop.
Add some oil to each divot, and let it get hot.
Fill each divot to the brim with batter.
Cook on one side until golden brown.
Flip the masa over, and cook on the other side until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve hot.

title: Nigerian Coco Pops
steps: Pour water into a bowl.
Stir in the coco pops, then the milk.
Serve warm.
procedure_text: Pour water into a bowl. Stir in the coco pops, then the milk. Serve warm.

title: Nigerian Coconut Rice
ingredient_lines: 4 tablespoons coconut oil or vegetable oil
steps: Rinse the rice and leave it to drain well.
Heat a skillet over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons coconut oil, then the diced onions. Cook, stirring, until softened slightly (about 2 minutes).
Stir in the thyme, ginger, and garlic. Cook for a few seconds.
Blend the pepper roughly then add spices and seasoning, salt stir for few minutes, then add fish and chicken
Stir in the rice and fry for about about 3 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, broth, bay leaf then stir
Cover and cook till firm to bite, about 15 minutes. Or more
When ready you can serve like that or any desired way.

title: Nigerian Cocoyam Chips
steps: Wash cocoyam with water, and peel the tuber. Rinse twice to remove dirt, then thinly slice it to your desired shape.
Put the sliced cocoyam in a pot, then season with salt. Toss well to season all of the cocoyam.
Preheat the frying pan enough vegetable oil for deep frying. Add the cocoyam slices, working in batches if needed, and fry until crisp.
Drain the cocoyam chips of excess oil, and serve.

title: Nigerian Coleslaw
steps: Slice cabbage thinly.
Use a grater to shred the carrot into a bowl. If possible, use a grater or mandoline that will make long, thin pieces.
Combine the cabbage and carrots. Add mayonnaise, and toss to combine.
Refrigerate until cold before serving.
procedure_text: Slice cabbage thinly. Use a grater to shred the carrot into a bowl. If possible, use a grater or mandoline that will make long, thin pieces. Combine the cabbage and carrots. Add mayonnaise, and toss to combine. Refrigerate until cold before serving.

title: Nigerian Corned Beef Sauce
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan. Add the onions, tomatoes, peppers, garlic, and ginger. Stir, and fry for about 10 minutes.
Mix in the corned beef, and fry for about 10 minutes.
Add salt and seasoning cube to taste. Stir, then cover and cook for a few minutes.
Adjust seasoning as needed, and serve.
procedure_text: Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan. Add the onions, tomatoes, peppers, garlic, and ginger. Stir, and fry for about 10 minutes. Mix in the corned beef, and fry for about 10 minutes. Add salt and seasoning cube to taste. Stir, then cover and cook for a few minutes. Adjust seasoning as needed, and serve.

title: Nigerian Custard
steps: Place the custard powder in a bowl. Stir in a small amount of cold water until smooth and lump-free.
Gradually stir in boiling water.
Allow the custard to set. If it is too thick or hard, stir in water to your desired consistency.
Stir in milk and sugar.
Serve.
procedure_text: Place the custard powder in a bowl. Stir in a small amount of cold water until smooth and lump-free. Gradually stir in boiling water. Allow the custard to set. If it is too thick or hard, stir in water to your desired consistency. Stir in milk and sugar. Serve.

title: Nigerian Dodo (Fried Ripe Plantain)
ingredient_lines: ½ cup puréed chile pepper mixed with tomatoes
steps: Cut each ripe plantain into 6 small pieces. Toss with salt and chile-tomato purée to taste.
Heat ½ cup of oil in a frying pan. Add the 6 plantain pieces, and deep fry until all sides are golden brown.
Serve with jollof rice or bean porridge.
procedure_text: Cut each ripe plantain into 6 small pieces. Toss with salt and chile-tomato purée to taste. Heat ½ cup of oil in a frying pan. Add the 6 plantain pieces, and deep fry until all sides are golden brown. Serve with jollof rice or bean porridge.

title: Nigerian Egg Pepper Soup
ingredient_lines: 2 bell peppers (red, green, or a combination), thinly sliced
1 teaspoon ground cayenne pepper (adjust to your preferred spice level)
Fresh cilantro or parsley, for garnish (optional)
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and minced garlic, and sauté until the onions become translucent and slightly golden.
Add the sliced bell peppers and chopped tomatoes to the saucepan. Cook for a few minutes until the vegetables start to soften.
In a separate bowl, crack the eggs and whisk them until well-beaten. Set aside.

Add the chicken or vegetable broth to the saucepan with the vegetables. Stir in the ground cayenne pepper, paprika, cumin, and coriander. Season with salt to taste. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Slowly pour the beaten eggs into the simmering soup, stirring gently with a wooden spoon or spatula in one direction. This will create thin strands of cooked egg throughout the soup.
Continue cooking the soup for about 3–4 minutes, allowing the egg to cook and thicken the soup slightly.
Taste the soup and adjust the seasoning if needed. Add more salt or spices according to your preference.
Once the soup is ready, remove it from the heat.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro or parsley if desired.

title: Nigerian Egg Roll
ingredient_lines: ½ cup evaporated milk or whole milk
steps: Combine the flour, baking powder, nutmeg, salt, and sugar in a bowl. Mix in the butter until crumbly. Mix in the egg and evaporated milk to make a dough.
Cover the dough with plastic wrap, and leave to rest for about 5–10 minutes.
While the dough is resting, preheat several inches of vegetable oil in a pot to 350–375°F (medium heat).
Divide the dough into six parts, flouring your palms to prevent the dough from sticking.

Flatten each piece of dough with your hands. Place one boiled egg on the dough, and wrap the dough around the egg to completely enclose it. Pinch the dough to tightly seal it around the egg. Repeat this process until all the eggs are wrapped.
Carefully transfer the egg rolls to the preheated oil, and fry until golden brown.
Remove the egg rolls from the oil, and place on paper towels to remove excess oil.
Serve with the drink of your choice.

title: Nigerian Egg Stew
steps: Heat palm oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Add the chile pepper, chopped onion, crushed Maggi cube, and salt. Stir and cook for 2–3 minutes.
In a separate bowl, beat the eggs. Pour into the pan and stir gently to scramble.
Cook for another 2–3 minutes, or until eggs are fully set but still moist.
Serve with boiled yam, cocoyam, or potatoes.
procedure_text: Heat palm oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the chile pepper, chopped onion, crushed Maggi cube, and salt. Stir and cook for 2–3 minutes. In a separate bowl, beat the eggs. Pour into the pan and stir gently to scramble. Cook for another 2–3 minutes, or until eggs are fully set but still moist. Serve with boiled yam, cocoyam, or potatoes.

title: Nigerian Eggplant Fufu
steps: Cut the eggplant into small pieces and soften in a pot of boiling water. Drain well.
Absorb excess water from the eggplant with paper towels, then blend with the food processor.
Transfer the eggplant purée to a pot, and stir over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Add the psyllium husk, and stir for additional 3 minutes.
Shape into desired portions.
procedure_text: Cut the eggplant into small pieces and soften in a pot of boiling water. Drain well. Absorb excess water from the eggplant with paper towels, then blend with the food processor. Transfer the eggplant purée to a pot, and stir over medium heat for 2 minutes. Add the psyllium husk, and stir for additional 3 minutes. Shape into desired portions.

title: Nigerian Ewa Agoyin
ingredient_lines: 4 cups brown beans or honey beans
steps: Cook the beans in plenty of water until they become extremely soft and mushy.
Stir or lightly mash the cooked beans until you get a smooth, thick, porridge-like texture. Season with salt to taste, and set aside.

Spoon the hot pepper sauce over the mashed beans and serve.

title: Nigerian Fried Cheese Curds (Wara)
steps: Strain the milk into a large pot.
Bring the milk to a boil over medium heat, stirring frequently.
Reduce the heat, and add lime juice. Do not stir. The curds should separate from the whey.
Pack the curds in a colander, and allow excess water to drain out.
Cut curds into desired shapes, and deep fry in hot oil.
procedure_text: Strain the milk into a large pot. Bring the milk to a boil over medium heat, stirring frequently. Reduce the heat, and add lime juice. Do not stir. The curds should separate from the whey. Pack the curds in a colander, and allow excess water to drain out. Cut curds into desired shapes, and deep fry in hot oil.

title: Nigerian Fried Noodles
steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the instant noodles, and cook until softened but still slightly firm.
Drain the noodles.
Heat a thin layer of vegetable oil in a frying pan. Add the onion, peppers, carrot, and leafy greens, and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Season the vegetables with stock cube or the instant noodle seasoning powder.
Add the cooked noodles to the vegetables, and stir-fry them until frothy.
Lower the heat so the noodles can fry more slowly for a few minutes.
Serve hot.
procedure_text: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the instant noodles, and cook until softened but still slightly firm. Drain the noodles. Heat a thin layer of vegetable oil in a frying pan. Add the onion, peppers, carrot, and leafy greens, and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Season the vegetables with stock cube or the instant noodle seasoning powder. Add the cooked noodles to the vegetables, and stir-fry them until frothy. Lower the heat so the noodles can fry more slowly for a few minutes. Serve hot.

title: Nigerian Fried Yam
ingredient_lines: Yam, peeled and sliced into sticks
steps: Rinse the cut yam and place in a bowl. Season with salt.
Heat oil in a pan or pot. Add the cut yam little by little to avoid overcrowding.
Stir, and cook until the yam is golden. Flip and cook until golden on all sides.
Remove fried yam from pan, and drain away any excess oil.
procedure_text: Rinse the cut yam and place in a bowl. Season with salt. Heat oil in a pan or pot. Add the cut yam little by little to avoid overcrowding. Stir, and cook until the yam is golden. Flip and cook until golden on all sides. Remove fried yam from pan, and drain away any excess oil.

title: Nigerian Fruit Skewer
steps: Cut all the fruit into small chunks.
Thread the fruit chunks onto a skewer.
procedure_text: Cut all the fruit into small chunks. Thread the fruit chunks onto a skewer.

title: Nigerian Jollof Rice
steps: Blend together the tomatoes, peppers, and the 2 large onions and set aside.
Boil, then deep-fry the meat. Set aside.
Put a 2-liter pot on the fire and allow any residual water in it to dry. Add the groundnut oil and let it heat up.
Add the diced onion and tomato purée. Stir constantly for 3–5 minutes then add the blended pepper mixture.
Add about 200 ml of the reserved meat stock, stock cubes, bay leaves, curry powder, thyme, cinnamon, ginger, garlic, and crayfish. Stir for about 10 minutes.
Add about 1.2 liters of water and allow to boil.
While waiting for the mixture to boil, wash the rice about 3–4 times or until the water is clear, then drain in a sieve.

When the pot boils, add the rice and season with salt. Use a wooden spatula to mix everything until you are sure that the rice is not just resting on one spot. Depending on the rice, you may need to add a little more water but remember to stir constantly with the wooden spatula in order to minimize the rice sticking to the bottom of the pot.
When you have attained your desired texture for the rice, reduce the heat to allow any residual water to be absorbed.
Serve and garnish with the fried beef/chicken.

title: Nigerian Miyan Giyada
ingredient_lines: 2–3 tablespoons palm oil or vegetable oil
2 cups leafy vegetables (e.g. spinach or ugu leaf)
steps: Season with onions, salt, and seasoning cubes, then boil until tender. Keep the stock.
Blend groundnuts (or use ready paste) until smooth.
Add the paste into the pot and allow it to cook, stirring to prevent burning.
Add pepper and a little palm oil or vegetable oil, then mix well.
Add your leafy vegetables and stir.
Allow the soup to cook until it thickens and oil begins to rise to the top. The soup should be thick, creamy, and rich with a nutty flavor.
Taste and add salt or seasoning if needed.
Serve with swallows like tuwo shinkafa or Tuwo dawa.
procedure_text: Season with onions, salt, and seasoning cubes, then boil until tender. Keep the stock. Blend groundnuts (or use ready paste) until smooth. Serve with swallows like tuwo shinkafa or Tuwo dawa.

title: Nigerian Oatmeal
steps: Soak the oats in enough milk or water overnight in the fridge.
Bring a pot of water to a boil with a pinch of salt. Stir in the soaked oats and a pinch of sugar.
Cook the oats, stirring, until they have absorbed the liquid and become soft.
Remove from the heat. Serve warm with banana, milk, and/or yogurt.
procedure_text: Soak the oats in enough milk or water overnight in the fridge. Bring a pot of water to a boil with a pinch of salt. Stir in the soaked oats and a pinch of sugar. Cook the oats, stirring, until they have absorbed the liquid and become soft. Remove from the heat. Serve warm with banana, milk, and/or yogurt.

title: Nigerian Ofe Akwu (Palm Fruit Soup)
ingredient_lines: 1 kilogram fresh palm fruits (or canned palm fruit concentrate)
700 grams assorted meat (e.g. beef, shaki, goat, oxtail)
1 tablespoon ogiri okpei (fermented locust bean paste)
150 grams uziza leaf or bitter leaf, shredded
steps: Boil the palm fruits in water for 20–25 minutes until soft, then drain. Pound the cooked fruits in a mortar to loosen the flesh from the seeds. Add warm water and squeeze the mixture through a sieve. Discard the fibre and seeds. If using canned concentrate, dilute as directed.
Season the meat with onion, 1 seasoning cube, and salt. Add stockfish midway through cooking. Cook on medium heat until tender. Reserve the meat stock.
Pour palm fruit extract into a pot. Cook on medium heat, stirring occasionally, until it thickens and oil rises to the surface about 15–20 minutes
Add ogiri okpei, ehuru, and puréed chiles. Stir well. Add reserved cooked meat and stock, smoked fish, ground crayfish, and the remaining seasoning cube. Stir and simmer on medium heat.
Taste and adjust with salt. The soup should be thick, rich, and deeply orange-red. If too thick, add a little warm water and stir.
Stir in uziza leaf. Cook for 3–5 minutes only. Serve hot with pounded yam (iyán), eba, or fufu.

title: Nigerian Palm Oil Boiled Yam (Ji Mmanu)
ingredient_lines: Fresh chile pepper, blended to paste
steps: Cook the yam pieces in salted boiling water for a few minutes.
Drain the yam pieces. Toss the yam with palm oil, salt, fresh pepper, and utazi leaves.
Serve.
procedure_text: Cook the yam pieces in salted boiling water for a few minutes. Drain the yam pieces. Toss the yam with palm oil, salt, fresh pepper, and utazi leaves. Serve.

title: Nigerian Pancakes
ingredient_lines: Dry ground cayenne pepper (to your taste)
steps: Break the eggs into a bowl, beat thoroughly, and mix with part of the water until well combined.
Sift the flour into the mixture, stir until smooth, then add the evaporated milk, sugar, and salt.
Gradually add the remaining water while mixing continuously to form a smooth, lump-free batter.
Heat a lightly oiled frying pan and pour in a thin layer of batter, spreading it evenly across the pan.
Cook on medium heat until the top sets, flip to fry the other side until golden brown, then repeat with the remaining batter.

title: Nigerian Peppered Turkey Wings
steps: Wash the turkey wings and put in a pot with 1 onion, garlic, ginger, stock cube, and thyme. Cover with water and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Cook until the water dries up, then bake in the oven at 200°C.
Blend the bell pepper and remaining onion to get a smooth paste.
Heat a small amount of vegetable oil in a pot. Add the pepper paste, and simmer until thickened and losing its raw flavor. Season with salt.
Add the turkey wings to the sauce, and toss to coat.

Add the pepper paste, and simmer until thickened and losing its raw flavor. Season with salt. Add the turkey wings to the sauce, and toss to coat.

title: Nigerian Pito
steps: Grind guinea corn into a powder.
Transfer ground guinea corn into a wide bowl, add enough water to fully cover. Stir well with a spatula.
Let the mixture rest until it settles into two phases. Drain the water away.
Pour the guinea corn slurry into a pot and bring to a boil.
After boiling, cool the mash and leave it to ferment for 1 day.
Boil mixture again for a few minutes over medium heat.
Set a sieve over a bowl, and pour the guinea corn mixture into it. Discard the solids.
Stir in sugar if desired, and allow pito to cool.
Serve cold over ice.

After boiling, cool the mash and leave it to ferment for 1 day. Boil mixture again for a few minutes over medium heat. Set a sieve over a bowl, and pour the guinea corn mixture into it. Discard the solids. Stir in sugar if desired, and allow pito to cool. Serve cold over ice.

title: Nigerian Puff Puff
steps: Sift the flour into a bowl, and mix in the nutmeg, yeast, sugar, and salt.

If using fresh or active-dry yeast, dissolve it in a small amount of warm water with a pinch of sugar. Let it get foamy before mixing it into the flour. If using instant yeast, mix it directly into the flour mixture.
Using your hands, mix small amounts of lukewarm water into the flour until all of the ingredients are thoroughly combined. The mixture should be smooth but not runny—i.e. it should not pour.
Cover the bowl with thin plastic film, and allow it to rise for about 45 minutes until doubled in volume.
Add oil to a deep pot to a depth of at least 3 inches.

Heat the oil over medium heat. Put a small piece of dough in the oil to see if it's hot enough—if the dough sizzles and rises to the surface of the oil, it is ready to fry the puff puff. If the oil isn't hot enough, the batter will sink to the bottom and remain there.
Roll the dough into small balls, and place into the oil. Make sure to fry in batches so that you don't overcrowd the oil and lower the temperature.

Flip the balls after the underside has gotten golden brown so that the topside may be fried as well. It can be difficult to control the balls when they keep flipping by themselves; in this case, just keep swirling until the puff puff is evenly golden.
Remove the puff puff from the oil when golden brown, and set them in a sieve lined with paper towels to drain away any excess oil.

title: Nigerian Rice and Beans Jollof
ingredient_lines: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil or palm oil
steps: Rinse the beans, and boil in water until tender. Drain the cooked beans.
Grind together the chiles, tomatoes, and onions to make a purée.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a pan, and add the purée. Season with stock cube and salt, and simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir in the parboiled rice and beans, and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve with beef, chicken, or moin-moin.
procedure_text: Rinse the beans, and boil in water until tender. Drain the cooked beans. Grind together the chiles, tomatoes, and onions to make a purée. Heat a thin layer of oil in a pan, and add the purée. Season with stock cube and salt, and simmer for 3 minutes. Stir in the parboiled rice and beans, and cook for 5 minutes. Serve with beef, chicken, or moin-moin.

title: Nigerian Roasted Plantain
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Place a rack on a baking sheet.
Place the plantains and fish on the rack.
Roast the plantains and fish in the preheated oven until they are cooked through. For an even roast, turn the plantains from time to time.
Heat the pepper stew, and serve it with the plantains and fish.
procedure_text: Heat the oven to 400°F. Place a rack on a baking sheet. Place the plantains and fish on the rack. Roast the plantains and fish in the preheated oven until they are cooked through. For an even roast, turn the plantains from time to time. Heat the pepper stew, and serve it with the plantains and fish.

title: Nigerian Roasted Yam
steps: Cut yam into suitably-sized pieces, then peel them.
Soak the yam in water overnight.
Rinse the yam and roast it, making sure all sides are deeply roasted.
Serve the roasted yam with groundnuts or roasted plantain.
procedure_text: Cut yam into suitably-sized pieces, then peel them. Soak the yam in water overnight. Rinse the yam and roast it, making sure all sides are deeply roasted. Serve the roasted yam with groundnuts or roasted plantain.

title: Nigerian Sardine Bread
steps: Sift the flour into a clean bowl. Add salt to taste, and mix everything together.
In another separate clean bowl, combine the warm water, sugar, yeast, and milk.
Transfer the flour mix into the yeast mix. Stir in the sardine oil, and mix it all together to make a dough.
Transfer the dough to a clean work surface, and knead it well.
Rub some soya oil in a clean bowl. Place the dough in the greased bowl, and turn it to make sure the oil coats the dough. Cover the dough, and proof for at least an hour until it doubles in volume.
Press on the dough to deflate it. Knead again, and roll it out.
Place the sardines one at a time inside the dough, and roll it up to enclose the sardines.
Line a baking pan with parchment paper. Place the dough inside the baking pan and proof for at least another 20 minutes.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Cool before cutting and serving.

title: Nigerian Smoked Fish
steps: Gut the fish and remove the gills. Wash well to remove any residual blood or guts.
Season the fish with a little bit of salt, and rub in the seasoning.
Bend the fish into a circle, with the fish tail inside of its mouth. Use a toothpick to secure the fish in this shape.
Wrap the prepared fish in aluminum foil.
Bake the fish for about 15 minutes.
Remove the foil from the fish. Set the oven to grill or broil, and broil the fish for about 10 minutes until browned.
Grease and preheat the grill.
Place the prepared fish on the grill, and cook until browned.

Remove the foil from the fish. Set the oven to grill or broil, and broil the fish for about 10 minutes until browned. Grease and preheat the grill. Place the prepared fish on the grill, and cook until browned.

title: Nigerian Tea (Hot Chocolate)
steps: Pour the evaporated milk into a mug, and stir in the chocolate drink mix.
Stir in hot water.
Serve with bread, Nigerian meat pie, or other Nigerian snacks.
procedure_text: Pour the evaporated milk into a mug, and stir in the chocolate drink mix. Stir in hot water. Serve with bread, Nigerian meat pie, or other Nigerian snacks.

title: Nigerian Tiger Nut Milk (Kunun Aya)
ingredient_lines: 1-inch (2.5 cm) piece of fresh ginger, peeled
Sweetener of choice (e.g., honey or sugar), to taste
steps: Rinse and soak the tiger nuts in 2 cups of water for at least 24 hours to soften.
Drain and blend the soaked tiger nuts with the dates and ginger, adding water as needed to form a smooth paste.
Strain the blended mixture using a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth to remove the chaff.
Dilute the extracted milk with the remaining water to the desired consistency.
Add your preferred sweetener to taste, and stir well.
Serve chilled. Refrigerate leftovers and consume within 1–2 days.
procedure_text: Rinse and soak the tiger nuts in 2 cups of water for at least 24 hours to soften. Dilute the extracted milk with the remaining water to the desired consistency. Add your preferred sweetener to taste, and stir well. Serve chilled. Refrigerate leftovers and consume within 1–2 days.

title: Nigerian Tomato Omelette
steps: Heat some oil in a pan over high heat. Add the tomatoes, and fry until well-heated.
Beat the eggs, and stir in the cooked tomato. Return the mixture to the pan over medium-low heat, making sure it is evenly spread across the pan. Cook until the egg is sturdy enough to flip.
Flip the omelette to the other side, and cook until the bottom is golden.
Serve hot with bread or jollof rice.

Flip the omelette to the other side, and cook until the bottom is golden. Serve hot with bread or jollof rice.

title: Nigerian Turmeric Rice
ingredient_lines: 1½ de Rica can of long-grain rice
steps: In a clean pot, combine chicken, stock cubes, half the onion, curry powder, and thyme. Cover with water, and cook until the chicken is tender.
Parboil the rice for about 10 minutes. Drain the rice in a sieve, and immediately rinse with cold water.
Transfer the chicken stock into a clean pot. Stir in the turmeric powder, black pepper, and curry powder. Cover, and bring to a boil.

Add the parboiled rice, making sure that the liquid is on the same level with the rice. Taste and add salt if necessary. Stir with a wooden spoon, and allow to cook on medium heat until the water is almost entirely dried up.
Add the chopped onions and tomatoes. Cover and continue to cook until the water dries up.
Stir to combine well, and serve.

Stir to combine well, and serve.

title: Nigerian Wheatbread Toast
steps: Crack the egg, and whisk it with a pinch of salt.
Spread some butter on the bread slices.
Spread some of the beaten egg on each slice of bread. Do not add so much egg that the bread is soaked.
Heat a nonstick pan over low heat, and add a thin layer of butter or oil.
Place the bread slices in the pan egg-side down. Sprinkle with yellow and black pepper.
Cook over low heat until the bread is dry and crisp. Remove from the heat.
Top the toast with the lettuce and sliced vegetables.
procedure_text: Crack the egg, and whisk it with a pinch of salt. Spread some butter on the bread slices. Spread some of the beaten egg on each slice of bread. Sprinkle with yellow and black pepper. Cook over low heat until the bread is dry and crisp. Remove from the heat. Top the toast with the lettuce and sliced vegetables.

title: Nigiri Sushi
steps: If making nigirizushi that requires a band of nori to hold the sushi together, cut the nori into strips about ¼ inch wide and long enough to wrap around the finished sushi with at least 1 inch (2.5 cm) of overlap. Place one such strip on the preparing surface.

Hand form the sushi rice into suitable sized sushi bases. Generally, this means a rectangular block about ½–1 inch wide, 1–1½ inch (2.5–4 cm) long, and ½–¾ inch (1.5–2 cm) high. It takes considerable experience to form pleasing sushi bases by hand (beginners may find a plastic sushi mold helpful for forming the bases). Wetting the hands in water prior to forming each sushi base keeps the rice from sticking to the hands.
For nigirizushi requiring wasabi between the rice and topping, add a small dab of wasabi on the rice.
Add the selected topping on top of the sushi rice.

If nori is used, wrap one of the nori band ends up and over the nigirisushi topping firmly, so that it sticks to the rice and topping. Wet the other nori band end with a small amount of water, and wrap it up and over the topping so that it overlaps the other nori end. The water causes the nori ends to stick together.

title: Nilagang Baka (Boiled Beef and Vegetables in Broth)
steps: Boil beef, peppercorns, onion, salt, corn, and potato until tender.
Slice onion chives into 3-inch strips. Add to the boiling beef.
Slice saba into half. Add to the boiling beef.
Serve in one large bowl or individual serving bowls.
Serve with rice on the side.
procedure_text: Boil beef, peppercorns, onion, salt, corn, and potato until tender. Slice onion chives into 3-inch strips. Add to the boiling beef. Slice saba into half. Add to the boiling beef. Serve in one large bowl or individual serving bowls. Serve with rice on the side.

title: Niçoise Salad
ingredient_lines: 200 g small fresh broad (fava) beans or green beans
12 small fresh artichokes, cut into rounds
12 anchovy fillets, or 300 g tuna steak
steps: Cut the tomatoes in quarters and salt them lightly once. Cut the eggs into quarters or slices. Cut the anchovies into 3–4 chunks (if using tuna, cut into similarly sized pieces). Peel the cucumber and finely slice it. Cut the green peppers into thin rings, and do the same with the onions.
Cut the garlic in two and rub the sides and bottom of a large salad bowl with it. Toss all the ingredients except the tomatoes into the bowl.
Drain the tomatoes, re-salt lightly and add to salad. In a separate bowl, mix 6 spoonfuls of olive oil with the basil, pepper, and salt and pour over salad. Refrigerate before serving.
procedure_text: Cut the tomatoes in quarters and salt them lightly once. Cut the eggs into quarters or slices. Cut the anchovies into 3–4 chunks (if using tuna, cut into similarly sized pieces). Toss all the ingredients except the tomatoes into the bowl. Drain the tomatoes, re-salt lightly and add to salad. In a separate bowl, mix 6 spoonfuls of olive oil with the basil, pepper, and salt and pour over salad. Refrigerate before serving.

title: Nkhwani wa Ndiwo (Malawian Vegetable Fritters)
ingredient_lines: 2 cups grated mixed vegetables (e.g. carrots, cabbage, onions, and green beans)
1 green chile (optional, for heat), finely chopped
steps: In a mixing bowl, combine the grated mixed vegetables, all-purpose flour, beaten egg, baking powder, and finely chopped green chili (if using).
Add the cornmeal to the mixture and mix well until everything is evenly combined.
Season the mixture with salt to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
In a frying pan, heat vegetable oil over medium-high heat.
Take spoonfuls of the vegetable mixture and carefully drop them into the hot oil. Flatten the fritters slightly with the back of the spoon.
Fry the fritters until they are golden brown and crispy on both sides. Use a slotted spoon to remove them from the oil and place them on paper towels to drain any excess oil.
Repeat the frying process with the remaining vegetable mixture.
Allow the fritters to cool slightly before serving.
procedure_text: In a mixing bowl, combine the grated mixed vegetables, all-purpose flour, beaten egg, baking powder, and finely chopped green chili (if using). Add the cornmeal to the mixture and mix well until everything is evenly combined. Season the mixture with salt to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference. In a frying pan, heat vegetable oil over medium-high heat. Take spoonfuls of the vegetable mixture and carefully drop them into the hot oil. Flatten the fritters slightly with the back of the spoon. Fry the fritters until they are golden brown and crispy on both sides. Use a slotted spoon to remove them from the oil and place them on paper towels to drain any excess oil. Repeat the frying process with the remaining vegetable mixture. Allow the fritters to cool slightly before serving.

title: Nkwobi (Nigerian Spicy Cow Foot)
steps: Cut the cow feet into small pieces, and remove all the bigger bones.
Place the cow feet in a pot, along with the salt, seasoning cubes, and chopped onions.
Add just enough water to cover the meat. Simmer until the meat is tender. Add small amounts of water as necessary, but there should be little to no liquid left in the pot once the meat is done.
In a separate pot, boil the ugba separately for just 3 minutes. Drain.
Dissolve the potash in a cup of water, and strain it into a separate pot. Add the palm oil to the potash water, and stir well until thick and yellow.
Add the crayfish, boiled ugba, Cameroon pepper, seasoning cube, and salt to the palm oil mixture. Stir well.
Add your cooked meat, and stir to coat with the palm oil mixture.
Serve in a wooden bowl with toppings of round-cut onions and sliced utazi leaves.

title: Nni Ede (Nigerian Pounded Cocoyam)
steps: Cut the cocoyam into small pieces. Rinse the pieces, and boil them for few minutes. Drain the cocoyam.
Mix water into the cassava flour to make a dough. Shape into balls.
Boil the cassava balls for few minutes, then drain.
Pound together the cassava balls and cocoyam until smooth and lump-free.
Serve with your choice of soup.

title: No-Bake Cheesecake
ingredient_lines: 200 g (7 oz) tennis biscuits or digestive biscuits, crushed to fine crumbs
540 g (19 oz) cream cheese, softened to room temperature
750 g (26.4 oz) tinned sweetened condensed milk
steps: Combine melted butter with biscuit crumbs. Press into a pie dish to make a crust.
Beat cream cheese until smooth and fluffy.
Beat lemon juice and condensed milk together.
Mix the condensed milk mixture into beaten cream cheese until thoroughly combined.
Pour filling into the prepared pie dish.
Refrigerate for minimum of 24 hours until set.
procedure_text: Combine melted butter with biscuit crumbs. Press into a pie dish to make a crust. Beat cream cheese until smooth and fluffy. Beat lemon juice and condensed milk together. Mix the condensed milk mixture into beaten cream cheese until thoroughly combined. Pour filling into the prepared pie dish. Refrigerate for minimum of 24 hours until set.

title: No-Bake Chocolate Cake
ingredient_lines: 2½ packs graham crackers, plain digestive biscuits, or whole wheat biscuits; crumbled
steps: Melt the margarine.
Mix the sugar and the egg.
Add the melted butter to the egg/sugar mixture.
Add the cocoa and the vanilla extract.
Add crumbled graham crackers. Mix well until all crackers are covered.
Line a cake pan with aluminum foil and pour in mixture.
Leave in refrigerator for 1 hour (preferably longer).
Unmold and serve.

title: No-Bake Chocolate Chip Cookie Pie
ingredient_lines: 1 package (15–18 oz/450 g) chocolate chip cookies (recipe uses 26 cookies)
1 ea. (9 oz/270 g) commercial graham cracker pie crust ("extra serving" or "deep dish" size)
1 container (8 oz/240 g) container frozen whipped topping, thawed
steps: Dip 8 cookies in milk, then place in a single layer in graham cracker crust. Top with one-third of the whipped topping.
Repeat the above step so that you have a total of 3 layers of cookies and whipped topping.
Crumble 2 chocolate chip cookies, and sprinkle over pie.
Cover and chill for 8 hours before serving.

title: No-Bake Chocolate Oatmeal Cookies
ingredient_lines: ½ cup smooth or chunky peanut butter
steps: Combine the sugar and cocoa in a saucepan, and stir well.
Add milk and stir well. Add butter and place over medium-high heat.
Bring mixture to a boil. When it reaches a rolling boil that cannot be stirred down, boil while stirring for exactly 1 minute.
Remove from heat and add peanut butter and vanilla. Stir until peanut butter is melted and mixture is smooth.
Add oatmeal and stir to combine. Immediately spoon the mixture onto a cookie sheet, leaving enough space between them for spreading out.
Let stand on counter for at least 20 minutes to stiffen or refrigerate to speed up the process.

title: No-Bake Matsa Cake
ingredient_lines: 2 ounces raisins, soaked in 1 tablespoon sweet red wine
½ lb butter, melted and cooled slightly
steps: Combine brown sugar, cocoa, soaked raisins, and melted butter.
Add this mixture to the crumbled matzah and mix well.
Divide the mixture into two 9-inch springform or other cake pans.
Knead the batter to create a flat and smooth surface.
Refrigerate for several hours.

title: No-Knead Bread
steps: In a large bowl, combine flour, yeast, and salt.
Add water and stir until you have a shaggy and sticky dough.
Cover bowl with plastic wrap. Let dough rest at least 12 hours, preferably 18 hours, at warm room temperature, about .
When the surface is dotted with bubbles, lightly flour a work surface or silicone mat and place dough on it.
Sprinkle it with a little more flour, and fold it over on itself once or twice.
Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let rest 15 minutes.
Using just enough flour to keep dough from sticking to the work surface and your fingers, gently and quickly shape the dough into a ball.
Generously coat a lint-free linen (i.e. not terrycloth) towel with flour.
Put the dough seam side-down on the towel and dust with more flour.
Cover with another lint-free linen towel and let rise for 2–3 hours. Dough will be more than double in size and will not readily spring back when poked with a finger.
At least half an hour before baking, place a 3–4-quart heavy covered pot (cast iron, enamel, Pyrex, or ceramic) in the oven and preheat to 450°F.
When the dough is ready, carefully remove the pot from the oven.
Slide your hand under the towel and turn the dough over into the pot. seam side up. It may look like a mess, but that's okay.
Shake the pan once or twice if the dough is unevenly distributed; it will straighten out as it bakes.
Cover with lid and bake 30 minutes.
Remove the lid and bake 15–30 minutes more, until the loaf is beautifully browned.
Remove the loaf from the pot and cool on a rack.

title: Nonpareil Sauce (Hartshorne)
ingredient_lines: 1 breast of roasted fowl, chopped fine
steps: Combine all the ingredients together.
Boil this mixture until warm and serve.
procedure_text: Combine all the ingredients together. Boil this mixture until warm and serve.

title: Noodles for Soup
steps: Beat the egg. Mix and knead in flour until you have a very stiff dough.
Roll the dough out into a thin sheet.
Sprinkle the dough with a good amount of flour to prevent it from sticking to itself. Tightly roll up the dough to make a log.
Use a sharp knife to cut the log cross-wise into thin slices, similar to how you would slice cabbage for slaw. Unroll the noodles and toss with flour.
Add the noodles to boiling soup. Simmer for 10 minutes.

title: North Carolina-Style BBQ Ribs
steps: Season ribs with Rib Rub and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Combine remaining ingredients and place in a spray bottle.
Place ribs in a 250°F smoker or a charcoal grill set for indirect heat at 250°F
Cook for 5–6 hours, spraying often with vinegar mixture.
Spray heavily with vinegar mixture and place on a high grill, turning and spraying constantly until well browned.
Remove and let rest 15 minutes; serve.

title: North Carolina Style BBQ Chicken
ingredient_lines: 3 each skinless bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
steps: Season chicken liberally with the barbecue rub. Gently massage into meat and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Meanwhile, combine the vinegar, honey, and Worcestershire sauce.
Place enough charcoal briquets to fill the charcoal compartment of a large chimney starter. Wad up some oil-moistened newspaper, stick under the compartment, and light. Wait 15 minutes.
Once coals are heated, disperse evenly along the bottom of the grill. Toss in soaked hickory chunks and reapply the grate.
Grill chicken over medium low, turning often and brushing with vinegar mixture when turned, until internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Remove and let rest for 7 minutes.
While chicken is resting, boil remaining vinegar mixture on high for 5 minutes. Drizzle over chicken and serve warm.

title: North Indian Fermented Bread (Batooru)
steps: Mix wheat flour and salt together. Add ghee and mix well so that there are no lumps and the ghee is evenly absorbed.
Add water in small amounts and knead well until the dough becomes soft and pliable.

When the dough is ready, form the dough into balls and roll them flat. Keep it slightly thick, unlike a bhatoora which is rolled to be very thin. Place the rolled batooru on a clean cloth and cover them with another moist cloth. Leave them covered overnight.
The next morning, take the batooru out from cloth and shallow fry them like a parantha.
Serve them hot, especially with with sabzi (spicy cooked vegetables), lassi, and mango pickles.

title: North Staffordshire Oatcakes
ingredient_lines: 220 g (1 cup or 8 oz) fine oatmeal
220 g (1 cup or 8 oz) wholemeal or plain flour
14 g (2 ½ tsp or ½ oz) fresh yeast
850 ml (3 ½ cups or 1 ½ pints) warm milk and water, mixed half and half
steps: Add the salt to the flour and oatmeal.
Dissolve the yeast with a little warm liquid and add the sugar. Allow the mixture to become frothy.
Mix the dry ingredients with the yeast liquid to make a batter.
Cover the batter with a clean cloth and leave it in a warm place for an hour.
Cook the oatcakes on a well-greased griddle. Put enough batter onto the griddle to produce an oatcake about 8–9 inches in diameter. The surface will be covered in holes as it cooks.
Flip the oatcake after 2–3 minutes when the upper side appears dry and the underneath is golden brown, and cook for another 2–3 minutes.

title: Nuked Nachos
ingredient_lines: About ⅓–½ cups (80–120 g) cheese (diced, grated, pre-melted, or similar)
steps: Spread the chips on a microwave-safe plate, and scatter the cheese on top.
Top the chips with any other desired microwave-safe toppings.
Microwave for 30 seconds, or until the cheese has melted. If the cheese melts onto the plate, just rip it off the plate and put it on the nachos.
Eat while hot!

title: Nune Soup
steps: Blend pepper the pepper to a paste. Boil it for few minutes.
Add the fish, locust beans, and salt to taste.
Stir and cook for few minutes.
Serve with pounded yam or akpu.

title: Nuremberg Gingerbread
steps: Bring the honey and sugar to the boil in a saucepan while stirring. Remove from the heat and let cool.
Sift the flour into a bowl.
Stir in the remaining ingredients.
Pour the honey mixture, then the baking powder into the flour. Stir and knead the dough until it cools down.
Roll out the dough.
Cut out the dough, and place on the gingerbread wafers.
Decorate with an almond, and transfer to a baking sheet.
Let cool for about a day
Bake at 180 °C for 15–20 minutes

title: Nutty Brownie Bars
ingredient_lines: 10 miniature chocolate coconut candy bars, chopped
steps: Prepare brownie mix according to package directions, reducing oil to 3 tablespoons.
Pour into lightly greased 9-by-3-inch pan.
Spread condensed milk over the brownie batter.
Sprinkle with chopped nuts and candy bars.
Bake at 350°F for 35–38 minutes or until done.
Cool completely and cut into bars.

title: Nutty Buddy Chocolate Cookie Bars
ingredient_lines: 1 cup pecan pieces or chopped pecans
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Place butter in microwave-safe dish, cover with a paper towel and microwave on high, for about 45 seconds, or until melted. Remove carefully and stir to melt completely.
Place the graham-cracker crumbs in a metal 13-by-9-inch baking pan.
Pour melted butter over crumbs, and stir and fold until all the crumbs are moistened with the butter. Press crumbs firmly and evenly into the bottom of the pan.
Pour the sweetened condensed milk over the crumb crust. Spread to the edges with the back of a spoon.
Top evenly with chocolate chips, pecans, and almonds. Press down with a fork.
Bake, uncovered, for 25–35 minutes or until bubbling slightly along the edges.
Remove from oven and cool to room temperature.
Refrigerate until firm for 1–2 hours before slicing.
Store at room temperature, covered with foil.

title: Nyama Choma (Tanzanian Barbecue)
ingredient_lines: 1 kg goat/lamb/beef/chicken meat, cut into thick chunks
1 heaped tbsp grated raw papaya for tenderness
steps: To keep the meat juicy and tender, clean it and preserve any extra fat on it. Place the meat in a glass or plastic dish.
Blend the remaining ingredients, then pour the resulting mixture over the meat.
Allow mixture to settle into the meat, then thoroughly massage it into the meat. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4–5 hours.
To bring the meat to room temperature for cooking, remove it from the refrigerator approximately an hour beforehand.
Light a charcoal grill and let it burn until the coals are completely covered with white ash.

Place a wire rack over the coals, add the meat, and cook until it has a little singe and color. To ensure equal cooking on all sides, turn meat frequently. Use a fresh brush and some oil or marinade to flavor the meat and keep it from drying out while it cooks.
To allow the inside of the meat to cook slowly and effectively, wrap it in a packet of foil. Or, keep grilling until the food is done to your liking.
Once the meat is done, use a sharp knife to cut it into bite-sized pieces.
Serve.

title: Nyama Yemombe (Zimbabwean Beef Stew)
ingredient_lines: 1 kg beef, washed and cut into bite-size cubes
1 beef stock cube or ½ teaspoon salt
steps: If the meat is tough, you can simmer it in salted water until tender (30–45 minutes), then drain and set aside.
In a large pot or pan, heat the oil over medium heat. Add onion, garlic, and ginger, and cook for 1 minute while stirring.
Add the beef to the pot. Fry for about 10 minutes until browned on all sides.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, then let them cook down until soft.
Add tomato paste, stock cube, paprika, and curry powder. Mix thoroughly.
Add water, cover the pot, and reduce heat to low. Let it simmer for 30–45 minutes, or until beef is soft and sauce has thickened.
Add chopped green pepper in the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Season with salt to taste.
Garnish with coriander, and serve with rice, porridge, or potato.

Reduce heat and cook for 4–6 minutes

steps: Put oats in a blender. Blend the oats to the finest powder you can get
Add as much of the water as possible to the blender. Blend some more.
Strain the mixture into a jug, and add the rest of the water.

title: Oat Porridge
ingredient_lines: ½ cup (45 g) rolled oats or other grain
steps: Mix oats and water, then bring to the boil, covered with a lid.
Once bubbling, stir and reduce temperature to the lowest possible to maintain simmering. Replace lid and watch carefully to prevent boiling over.
Stir every minute or so. After five minutes, remove lid, stir thoroughly and add milk.
Mix through, and keep stirring until fully mixed.
Serve and add raisins, sugar, brown sugar, maple syrup, a pinch of salt, honey or inverted sugar syrup to taste.

title: Oat Rice
steps: Wash the rice and drain the water.
Pour the oat milk and rice into a pot.
Put the pot on the stove, and cook over medium heat for about 5 minutes or until foam appears.
Start stirring the mixture with a spoon, and continue stirring until the mixture boils.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, stirring, until almost all the liquid is gone.
Remove from the heat and serve.

title: Oaties
steps: Put the butter or margarine, sugar, and treacle into a saucepan. Stir over low heat until the fat and sugar have melted.
Add the oats, flour, and baking powder and combine thoroughly.
Press into two well greased 7-inch round cake tins.
Bake in the centre of a moderate oven at 180°C (350°F / gas mark 4) for 20–25 minutes or until cooked through (test with a skewer).
Mark into slices whilst warm.
Allow to become almost cold in the tin before removing.

title: Oatmeal Banana Waffle
steps: Turn waffle iron on high.
Put all ingredients in a blender and blend on high until the contents are smooth. Let the mixture sit for 10–15 minutes.
Spray the waffle iron with non-stick cooking spray.
Pour some of the batter onto the waffle iron. Cook for about 10 minutes. Repeat until you are out of batter.

title: Oatmeal Chocolate Chip Cookies I
steps: In a large bowl beat eggs lightly to break the yolks, then mix in the shortening—you should have a loose mixture.
Mix in the brown sugar, milk, vanilla, and salt.
Mix the flour, baking powder, soda, cinnamon, and oatmeal together in another bowl.
Mix the wet and dry mixes together to get a soft dough.
Stir in chocolate chips and walnuts.
Make balls and place onto a greased or parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake in an oven prheated to 180°C (350°F) for 15–20 minutes.

title: Oatmeal Chocolate Chip Cookies II
ingredient_lines: 3 sticks (12 oz / 340 g) butter, softened to room temperature
Add more chocolate chips (or other small candy) if desired.
Substitute other "filler" (wheat germ, flaxseed, nuts, seeds, etc.) for some of the oatmeal.
Whatever you do to adjust the chocolate chips and oatmeal, make sure the resulting dough is very stiff—this helps make the cookies chewy.
steps: Cream butter and both kinds of sugar with an electric mixer until smooth.
Combine the water, eggs, and vanilla in a separate container.
Gradually beat the egg mixture into the butter mixture until smooth.
Combine the flour and baking soda, then sift this mixture into the butter mixture. Mix to form a dough.
Use a sturdy mixing spoon to stir in the chocolate chips and 6 cups of the oats.
Stir in additional oats until the dough is stiff and almost crumbly.
If desired, chill dough until ready to bake.
Scoop teaspoon-sized balls of dough and place on a greased or parchment-lined cookie sheet.
Bake in a preheated 350°F (175C) oven for about 10 minutes, until a toothpick inserted into the cookies comes out clean.
procedure_text: Cream butter and both kinds of sugar with an electric mixer until smooth. Combine the water, eggs, and vanilla in a separate container. Gradually beat the egg mixture into the butter mixture until smooth. Combine the flour and baking soda, then sift this mixture into the butter mixture. Mix to form a dough. Use a sturdy mixing spoon to stir in the chocolate chips and 6 cups of the oats. Stir in additional oats until the dough is stiff and almost crumbly. If desired, chill dough until ready to bake. Scoop teaspoon-sized balls of dough and place on a greased or parchment-lined cookie sheet. Bake in a preheated 350°F (175C) oven for about 10 minutes, until a toothpick inserted into the cookies comes out clean.

title: Oatmeal Chocolate Chip Cookies III
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Cream together butter and sugars.
Add egg and vanilla and mix.
Add salt, baking soda, and flour; mix.
Mix in oatmeal.
Mix in chocolate chips.
Scoop cookies onto a greased or parchment-lined baking sheet.
Bake 9–11 minutes at 375°F.
procedure_text: Preheat oven to 375°F. Cream together butter and sugars. Add egg and vanilla and mix. Add salt, baking soda, and flour; mix. Mix in oatmeal. Mix in chocolate chips. Scoop cookies onto a greased or parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake 9–11 minutes at 375°F.

title: Oatmeal Cookies I
steps: Using a mixer, cream together the shortening, brown sugar, white sugar, egg, water and vanilla until light and fluffy (about 10 minutes on high).
In a mixing bowl, mix together the oats, flour, baking soda, and salt.
Add dry ingredients into wet, mix well using mixer.
Stir in raisins if using.
Scoop the portions out—this recipe makes 20 cookies, so make 20 portions.
Bake at 350°F (180°C) for 8–10 minutes.
procedure_text: Using a mixer, cream together the shortening, brown sugar, white sugar, egg, water and vanilla until light and fluffy (about 10 minutes on high). In a mixing bowl, mix together the oats, flour, baking soda, and salt. Add dry ingredients into wet, mix well using mixer. Stir in raisins if using. Scoop the portions out—this recipe makes 20 cookies, so make 20 portions. Bake at 350°F (180°C) for 8–10 minutes.

title: Oatmeal Cookies II
steps: Put the oil, sugar, water, and vanilla together in a bowl. Mix well.
Add the oats, flour, salt, and baking soda.
Place on a greased baking sheet in lumps about 1 inch across and about 3 inches apart.
Bake at 191 °C (375 °F) for 10–12 minutes, and serve when the cookies have begun to brown.
procedure_text: Put the oil, sugar, water, and vanilla together in a bowl. Mix well. Add the oats, flour, salt, and baking soda. Place on a greased baking sheet in lumps about 1 inch across and about 3 inches apart. Bake at 191 °C (375 °F) for 10–12 minutes, and serve when the cookies have begun to brown.

title: Oatmeal Muffins
steps: Stir rolled oats and buttermilk together in a mixing bowl.
Combine flour, coconut, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in another mixing bowl. Stir together to mix. Make a well in the center.
Add egg and margarine to oat mixture. Mix well.
Pour all at once into flour mixture. Stir just to moisten.
Fill muffin cups ¾ full.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 15–20 minutes.
procedure_text: Stir rolled oats and buttermilk together in a mixing bowl. Combine flour, coconut, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in another mixing bowl. Stir together to mix. Make a well in the center. Add egg and margarine to oat mixture. Mix well. Pour all at once into flour mixture. Stir just to moisten. Fill muffin cups ¾ full. Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 15–20 minutes.

title: Oatmeal Raisin Cookies
ingredient_lines: ¾ cup butter, applesauce, equal parts butter and vegetable oil, or shortening
1 ¼ cup brown sugar, firmly packed
3 cup raw oats (rolled or quick/old fashioned)
steps: Heat oven to 350°F.
Lightly grease cookie sheet with oil, shortening, or butter.
Combine your choice of fat (butter, apple sauce, butter/vegetable oil mix, or shortening), brown sugar, egg, milk, and vanilla; beat with mixer on high speed to blend well.
Combine oats, flour, baking soda, salt and cinnamon; add to shortening mixture and combine until just blended.
Stir in raisins and nuts.
Drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet, 2 inches apart.
Bake for 10–13 minutes, or until lightly browned.
procedure_text: Heat oven to 350°F. Lightly grease cookie sheet with oil, shortening, or butter. Combine your choice of fat (butter, apple sauce, butter/vegetable oil mix, or shortening), brown sugar, egg, milk, and vanilla; beat with mixer on high speed to blend well. Combine oats, flour, baking soda, salt and cinnamon; add to shortening mixture and combine until just blended. Stir in raisins and nuts. Drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet, 2 inches apart. Bake for 10–13 minutes, or until lightly browned.

title: Oatmeal Stout Brownies
ingredient_lines: 6 tablespoons unsalted room temperature butter, cut into cubes
1 ½ cup superfine or granulated sugar
1 ¼ cups (10 ounces) oatmeal stout beer (room temperature)
⅓ cup superfine or granulated sugar
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Line a 9 x 13-inch baking pan with nonstick foil (or grease and flour, or parchment paper…your call).
In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, cocoa powder, and salt until evenly combined. Set aside.
Melt butter, bittersweet chocolate, and white chocolate chips in a double-boiler over very low heat, stirring constantly until melted. Remove from heat.
In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs and sugar on high speed until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Add melted chocolate mixture, beating until combined.

Beat reserved flour mixture into melted chocolate mixture. Whisk in stout beer. The batter will seem a bit thin. Pour into prepared baking pan. Drop semisweet chocolate chips evenly on top of batter (some will sink in).
Beat cream cheese in medium bowl with electric mixer on medium speed until smooth. Gradually beat in sugar. Beat in vanilla and 1 egg just until blended.
Pour cream cheese mixture over brownie batter in pan; cut through mixture with knife several times for marbled design.
Bake for 25–35 minutes on center rack in the oven, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out almost clean.
Let brownies cool, uncovered, to room temperature. Dust with confectioners' sugar before serving if desired.

Beat reserved flour mixture into melted chocolate mixture. Whisk in stout beer. The batter will seem a bit thin. Pour into prepared baking pan. Drop semisweet chocolate chips evenly on top of batter (some will sink in). Beat cream cheese in medium bowl with electric mixer on medium speed until smooth. Gradually beat in sugar. Beat in vanilla and 1 egg just until blended. Pour cream cheese mixture over brownie batter in pan; cut through mixture with knife several times for marbled design. Bake for 25–35 minutes on center rack in the oven, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out almost clean. Let brownies cool, uncovered, to room temperature. Dust with confectioners' sugar before serving if desired.

title: Obe Eja Kika (Nigerian Smoked Fish Stew)
steps: Coarsely grind the tomatoes, habanero pepper, tatashe, green bell peppers, and onions.
Heat the palm oil and vegetable oil in a pot. Add the ground pepper mix, and cook, stirring, for about 10–15 minutes.
Stir in the fish seasoning powder, shrimp powder, salt, and stock cube. Add the panla fish, and stir.
Add some water to loosen up the stew, stir, and simmer for 10–15 minutes on low heat.
Stir in the scent leaf, and remove from the heat.
Serve with rice, pasta, or boiled yam.
procedure_text: Coarsely grind the tomatoes, habanero pepper, tatashe, green bell peppers, and onions. Heat the palm oil and vegetable oil in a pot. Add the ground pepper mix, and cook, stirring, for about 10–15 minutes. Stir in the fish seasoning powder, shrimp powder, salt, and stock cube. Add the panla fish, and stir. Add some water to loosen up the stew, stir, and simmer for 10–15 minutes on low heat. Stir in the scent leaf, and remove from the heat. Serve with rice, pasta, or boiled yam.

title: Obuwunga (Ugandan Traditional Bread)
steps: In a bowl, combine the millet flour or cornmeal with the salt.

Gradually add water to the flour, mixing it with a mixing stick or spoon until it forms a smooth and thick dough. The amount of water needed may vary, so add it gradually until the right consistency is achieved.
Once the dough is ready, form it into a round or oval shape, smoothing the surface with wet hands.
In a pot, add some water and place a steaming rack at the bottom. Alternatively, you can use banana leaves to line the pot to prevent sticking.
Carefully place the shaped dough on the steaming rack or banana leaves.
Cover the pot with a lid and steam the bread over medium heat for about 30–40 minutes, or until the bread is cooked and firm.
Remove the bread from the pot and let it cool for a few minutes before serving.
Serve with various stews and dishes, using the bread to scoop up the stews.

title: Ofe Onugbu (Bitter Leaf Soup)
ingredient_lines: 300 g assorted meat (beef, tripe, cow skin)
1 tablespoon ogiri or iru (fermented locust beans, optional)
3–5 small cocoyam pieces or 2 tablespoons achi powder (as thickener)
steps: Wash the bitter leaves thoroughly, squeezing and rinsing several times to reduce the bitterness. Set aside.
In a pot, combine the assorted meat, stockfish, dryfish, salt, seasoning cubes, and chopped onions. Cover with water, and simmer until the meat is tender.
Add palm oil and allow it to melt into the meat stock.
If using cocoyam, boil it separately, peel, blend into a paste, and stir into the soup as a thickener. If using achi or ofor powder, stir directly into the pot.
Stir in the ground crayfish, pepper, ogiri, and ground crayfish.
Stir in the washed bitter leaves.Allow to simmer for 5–10 minutes until the soup thickens and the flavors combine.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
procedure_text: Wash the bitter leaves thoroughly, squeezing and rinsing several times to reduce the bitterness. Set aside. Add palm oil and allow it to melt into the meat stock. If using cocoyam, boil it separately, peel, blend into a paste, and stir into the soup as a thickener. If using achi or ofor powder, stir directly into the pot. Stir in the ground crayfish, pepper, ogiri, and ground crayfish. Stir in the washed bitter leaves.Allow to simmer for 5–10 minutes until the soup thickens and the flavors combine. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

title: Ofe Owerri
ingredient_lines: 1 kg assorted meat (beef, goat, cow tripe, etc.)
500 g dryfish, smoked fish, or stockfish
Fresh bell pepper or chile pepper
1 cup okazi or uziza leaves, thinly sliced
steps: Clean the meats and dryfish, and cut into pieces.
Simmer the meat with seasoning cubes and water in a pot until tender. Add stockfish and dried fish.
Stir in the cocoyam paste to thicken the soup, making sure it's well incorporated.
Stir in the palm oil, crayfish, ogiri, and pepper. Simmer for 5–10 minutes.
Add okazi leaves, and simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir in ugu leaves, and simmer for 2–3 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve hot with pounded yam or fufu.
procedure_text: Clean the meats and dryfish, and cut into pieces. Simmer the meat with seasoning cubes and water in a pot until tender. Add stockfish and dried fish. Stir in the cocoyam paste to thicken the soup, making sure it's well incorporated. Stir in the palm oil, crayfish, ogiri, and pepper. Simmer for 5–10 minutes. Add okazi leaves, and simmer for 3 minutes. Stir in ugu leaves, and simmer for 2–3 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve hot with pounded yam or fufu.

title: Ogolale (Mashed Yam and Plantain)
steps: Boil the yam and plantain in a pot of salted water until cooked through.
Drain the water, and transfer the cooked yam and plantain to a clean container.
Use a spoon or spatula to mash the yam and plantain.
Mix in the palm oil.
Adjust seasoning to taste, and serve.
procedure_text: Boil the yam and plantain in a pot of salted water until cooked through. Drain the water, and transfer the cooked yam and plantain to a clean container. Use a spoon or spatula to mash the yam and plantain. Mix in the palm oil. Adjust seasoning to taste, and serve.

title: Okpa (Boiled Bambara Bean Pudding)
ingredient_lines: Banana leaves or food- and heat-safe plastic bags
3 cigar cups (450 g / 1 lb) of okpa flour (ground bambara beans)
steps: Thoroughly wash the banana leaves using water and salt.
Sift the okpa flour into a large bowl, and mix in the crushed stock cubes and salt. Add the palm oil, and mix very well with a wooden spoon.

Start adding the lukewarm water to the mixed okpa flour, mixing very well until there are no lumps. After ensuring that there are no lumps, add enough lukewarm water so that the okpa will not be hard as stone when it is done.
Stir in the sliced habanero pepper, and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Scoop some okpa mixture into transparent nylon or banana leaves—avoid adding too much—and tie them closed.
Set some water to boil on the stove in a big pot. Ensure the water is boiling before putting in your okpa.
Boil the okpa for about 1 hour before checking it. The okpa will be solid when fully cooked.
Serve with custard, oatmeal, or pap.

Add the palm oil, and mix very well with a wooden spoon. Start adding the lukewarm water to the mixed okpa flour, mixing very well until there are no lumps. title: Okpo Ogede (Plantain Moi-Moi)
ingredient_lines: 1 teaspoon palm oil or to taste
steps: Blend the plantains, plantain flour, onion, and crayfish together with a little water.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl, then mix in salt and palm oil.
Divide the mixture between molds, such as ramekins or aluminum pouches.
Place the filled molds in a steamer basket over boiling water. Cook until set.
Serve with custard, oatmeal, and/or cooked ground corn (akamu).
procedure_text: Blend the plantains, plantain flour, onion, and crayfish together with a little water. Transfer the mixture to a bowl, then mix in salt and palm oil. Divide the mixture between molds, such as ramekins or aluminum pouches. Place the filled molds in a steamer basket over boiling water. Cook until set. Serve with custard, oatmeal, and/or cooked ground corn (akamu).

title: Okra Plantain Porridge
steps: Combine the plantain and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 3–5 minutes.
Add the catfish, stock cube, onions, palm oil, okra, and ugu leaves. Stir until a porridge is formed, then cook for an additional 5 minutes.
Season with the salt and chile-tomato. Serve hot.
procedure_text: Combine the plantain and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 3–5 minutes. Add the catfish, stock cube, onions, palm oil, okra, and ugu leaves. Stir until a porridge is formed, then cook for an additional 5 minutes. Season with the salt and chile-tomato. Serve hot.

title: Olive Oil Bread
steps: In a large bowl mix together the warm water, yeast, sugar, salt, and olive oil.
Stir in 2 cups of the flour in order to make a soft ball.
Knead in additional flour so that dough is soft and not sticky.
Place kneaded dough in a medium size greased bowl. Cover and let rise until doubled in size.
Punch down dough, and form into ball or loaf shape.
Place onto a greased cookie sheet. Cover and let rise for 15–20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 375° F (190°C).
Bake in the preheated oven for 30–40 minutes, until golden brown.
For a glazed, shiny effect, brush one egg white and one tablespoon of water (mixed) onto the bread 5 minutes before completion.
procedure_text: In a large bowl mix together the warm water, yeast, sugar, salt, and olive oil. Stir in 2 cups of the flour in order to make a soft ball. Knead in additional flour so that dough is soft and not sticky. Place kneaded dough in a medium size greased bowl. Cover and let rise until doubled in size. Punch down dough, and form into ball or loaf shape. Place onto a greased cookie sheet. Cover and let rise for 15–20 minutes. Preheat the oven to 375° F (190°C). Bake in the preheated oven for 30–40 minutes, until golden brown. For a glazed, shiny effect, brush one egg white and one tablespoon of water (mixed) onto the bread 5 minutes before completion.

title: Omelette of Breadcrumbs
steps: Beat the eggs, adding finely chopped garlic and parsley successively.
Add breadcrumbs, making sure the mixture is uniform.
Cook the omelette over low heat with a few drops of cooking oil to prevent sticking.
procedure_text: Beat the eggs, adding finely chopped garlic and parsley successively. Add breadcrumbs, making sure the mixture is uniform. Cook the omelette over low heat with a few drops of cooking oil to prevent sticking.

title: Omo tuo
steps: After properly cleaning the rice, add it to a saucepan of water. When the rice is tender, add salt and bring to a boil. Give it a good five to seven minutes.
To make the rice smooth, mash it with a wooden spoon or a small pestle.
Pour cold water into a cup and place it near the pan. Transfer the rice to a serving dish after scooping it with wet hands and rolling it into balls.
procedure_text: After properly cleaning the rice, add it to a saucepan of water. When the rice is tender, add salt and bring to a boil. Give it a good five to seven minutes. To make the rice smooth, mash it with a wooden spoon or a small pestle. Pour cold water into a cup and place it near the pan. Transfer the rice to a serving dish after scooping it with wet hands and rolling it into balls.

title: Omu Tuo (Ghanian Mashed Rice)
steps: If desired, rinse the rice well to eliminate excess starch. This step is optional as the starch contributes to the desired stickiness of the rice.
Combine the rice, butter, and salt in a pot with water. Cook over low heat, allowing the rice to slowly simmer until all the water is absorbed and the rice reaches a soft texture.
Using a wooden spoon, begin pounding the rice in the pot, alternating from one side to the other. Repeat this process until the rice transforms into a mushy consistency.
Transfer the mashed rice to a moistened bowl and gently swirl it until a bowl shape is formed.
Serve with peanut stew or any other soup of your preference

title: One-Hour Thanksgiving Dinner
ingredient_lines: 1 ea. 5–6 lb fully pre-cooked smoked turkey breast (see notes)
1–2 package(s) of instant potatoes or stuffing
Nonstick cooking spray or vegetable oil
steps: Thaw the frozen turkey breast for one day in the refrigerator.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Remove turkey from bag and place in aluminum roasting pan. Spray the turkey with cooking spray, or rub the breast with it vegetable oil.
Place turkey breast in the oven on the middle rack, and cook for 15 minutes.
Begin preparing the gravy mix according to package directions.
Place the vegetables on the stove over low heat.
Prepare the instant potatoes or stuffing according to the package directions.
On a small pan lay out your frozen biscuits allowing them to touch one another. At this point the turkey breast should have been cooking for 30 minutes.

Place the frozen biscuits on the lower rack of the oven. The biscuits will cook just fine with the turkey in the oven and will be ready in 25–30 minutes. Check them after 20 minutes to be sure they do not burn.
Finish preparing your instant potatoes or stuffing, instant gravy, and vegetables. Place them in serving dishes if desired.

Place the cranberry sauce in a serving dish. If you are serving pie along with the dinner you will also need to place the pie on a serving dish. If a frozen pie has been purchased, follow the instructions for reheating
After 1 hour of cooking, remove the turkey and check the internal temperature with a thermometer to make sure it has reached 160°F (the minimum temperature necessary to kill any remaining bacteria).
Carve the turkey and serve with all of the prepared side dishes.
